plain.li: Sat by the hearth with {X_nameDef} tonight. We passed the poker back and forth and hardly spoke.
{X_nameDef} says {X_possessive} people keep one fire going all winter and never let it out. I banked ours extra carefully tonight.
[cold] {X_nameDef} came in frozen. By the time {X_possessive} boots stopped steaming, we were friends.
[rain] Chestnuts by the hearth with {X_nameDef} while it poured. A good night.

warm.li: Gave the visitor the seat nearest the fire and the thickest blanket we had.

blunt.li: Hearth, a visitor, a quiet evening. Fine.

cheerful.li: {X_nameDef} and I roasted chestnuts and burned most of them! Still good.

gloomy.li: {X_nameDef} stared into the fire like someone who'd lost a lot. I didn't ask.

cold.li: {X_nameDef} talks more by a fire. Learned a fair amount about the roads east.

plain.li: Dessert after supper. I ate it slowly and licked the plate.
Somebody baked today, and it was gone about as fast as it was served.
[fall] Sweets from the new harvest. The kitchen smelled of it all afternoon.
Sweets on an ordinary day, for no reason anyone would tell me.
[child] I had dessert and got it all over my face and I didn't share.
[winter] Hot dessert on a cold night. I ate it standing by the oven.
[work:Cooking] Baked today. Burned my wrist on the oven door and didn't care. It came out right.

warm.li: Saved the last slice for whoever came in late. I thought about it the whole evening.

cheerful.li: Dessert tonight! I'd forgotten how much I missed sugar.

gloomy.li: Dessert. The one good thing in a long week.

cold.li: Sweets lift everyone's mood for the price of some flour and fruit. We should bake more often.

plain.li: Supper from the big pot, thick enough to stand a spoon in.
Soup and bread for supper. Not fancy, and I had two bowls.
[winter] Soup hot enough to burn. The best thing about winter is the soup.
[bad] Weak stew again. More water than stew.
[work:Hunting] Meat in the pot tonight that I brought in myself. Tastes better that way.
[rain] Rain all day, and the soup pot going all day. Everybody came in wet and went out warm.
Whatever went in the pot today, there was plenty of it, and I had two bowls.

warm.li: Somebody kept the pot going all day so whoever came in could eat. I came in at dusk and it was still hot.

gloomy.li: Same pot, same supper. It's warm, at least.

cold.li: One pot feeds everyone and wastes nothing. Sensible cooking.

plain.li: Slop from the slop pot. Gray, warm, and not something I'd describe to anyone.
A bowl of slop for supper. I ate it fast so I wouldn't have to look at it.
[afterraid] The day after the raid, slop. The cooks didn't have it in them.
[child] The gray stuff again. I hid half of mine under the table.

warm.li: Slop for supper. The cook looked so tired I said it was fine.

cheerful.li: Supper was slop! Well. It's food.

gloomy.li: Slop. I ate it all and didn't notice until the bowl was empty.

cold.li: The slop keeps us alive. That's all it's for.

plain.li: [good] Cheese from the press, sharp enough to make my eyes water. Good cheese.
[good] Grilled cheese on bread. I could live on that.
[bad] Tried the new cheese. It needed more time, or less of whatever went into it.
[bad] The cheese has gone wrong somewhere. It smells like the pens.
[good,winter] Cheese and bread at the hearth. Winter food.
[good,skill:Cooking] The cheese I pressed in spring is ready, and it's good. I may have bragged.

warm.li: [good] Cut a wedge of cheese for whoever was nearest, and then one for whoever was next.

blunt.li: [bad] Bad cheese. Somebody should learn to make it properly.

cheerful.li: [good] The cheese is ready! It's the best thing we've ever made.

gloomy.li: [bad] Even the cheese is against me today.

cold.li: [good] Cheese keeps for months and sells well. Good use of the milk.

plain.li: [good] A cup of the colony's wine after supper. It has come along well since spring.
[good] Steak with wine tonight. I didn't think we lived like that out here.
[bad] The wine has turned. Drank it anyway, and wished I hadn't.
[bad] Sour wine. Whoever minds the barrels should taste it before pouring.
[good,evening] Wine on the step at dusk, watching the light go off the fields.
[good,trait:Teetotaler] Tasted the wine to be polite. It was good, which annoyed me.

warm.li: [good] Opened a bottle with friends tonight. We toasted the ones who aren't here.

blunt.li: [bad] The wine is vinegar. Fix the barrels.

cheerful.li: [good] The wine is good this year! Somebody stop me before I write a song about it.

gloomy.li: Drank wine to forget the week. The week is still here.

cold.li: [good] Good wine is worth more than silver to the right buyer. We should keep some back.

plain.li: A full mug at the end of the day. I'd earned it.
A drink with supper. It tasted the way summer smells.
[evening] A full mug, the long table, and nobody in a hurry to go to bed.
[work:Growing] Brought in the barley this morning and drank last year's barley tonight. That's how it should go.
[winter] Drank it warmed, with spice in it. My hands finally warmed up.

warm.li: Bought the next round, so to speak. Ale's free here, but the gesture counts.

cheerful.li: Somebody started singing over the mugs tonight, and I think it was me.

gloomy.li: Ale helps. Not much, and not for long.

cold.li: One mug of ale, no more. A clear head in the morning matters more.

plain.li: Meat with char on it for lunch. My fingers still smell of smoke.
Meat off the fire tonight, burnt at the ends, which is the best part.
[bad] Dried meat again. Like chewing a boot.
[winter] Meat from the fall hanging. That's what it was for.
Ate it off a stick, standing up in the yard.

warm.li: Gave half my meat to the one beside me, who'd missed lunch.

cheerful.li: Meat off the fire! The best kind of night.

gloomy.li: Dried meat and water. Supper of kings.

cold.li: Smoked meat keeps all winter. Worth every hour at the smoker.

plain.li: An hour in the library with a candle and a book about rivers. I don't care about rivers. I read the whole thing.
Read in the library today. Quiet, and it smells of paper and wax.
[skill:Intellectual] Found a book in the library I'd missed. Copied out a page of it.
[rain] Rain drumming outside, and a book in the library. Perfect.
[child] I read a book in the library all by myself. It had pictures of a dragon.

warm.li: Read aloud in the library to whoever wanted to listen. Two stayed until the end.

cheerful.li: The library is my favorite room! You're not allowed to shout in it.

gloomy.li: The library is the only room where nobody needs anything from me.

cold.li: I've noted who uses the library and who never sets foot in it.
